docs.summary: The CPU image work an import does before storing a texture: sizing, normal maps, alpha and mip chains. Every image is RGBA8 with its bottom row first, as textures hold them.
Whether any pixel is less than opaque.

members.name: FitMaxSize
members.signature: public static byte[] FitMaxSize(byte[] pixels, ref int width, ref int height, int maxSize, bool srgb)

docs.summary: Halves the image until neither side exceeds `maxSize`.

members.name: Downsample
members.signature: public static byte[] Downsample(byte[] source, ref int width, ref int height, bool srgb)

docs.summary: Halves an image with a two by two box. At odd sizes the last row or column is left out, as the mip sizes round down. sRGB colour is averaged as light rather than as stored values, as the GPU does for an sRGB mip chain.

members.name: BuildMipChain
members.signature: public static List<byte[]> BuildMipChain(byte[] level0, int width, int height, MipChainOptions options)

docs.summary: Every level from `level0` down to one pixel, each filtered from the one above.
Rebuilds each normal from its X and Y at unit length, as the shaders read it, which averaging shortens.

members.name: NormalsFromHeight
members.signature: public static void NormalsFromHeight(byte[] pixels, int width, int height, float bumpiness, bool smooth)

docs.summary: Replaces the image with the normals of its brightness as a height field, tiling at the edges. Smooth takes the slope across three by three texels, sharp across the nearest two.
Inverts green, turning a Y down normal map into the Y up one Prowl reads.
Sets alpha to the brightness of each pixel.

members.name: ToSingleChannel
members.signature: public static void ToSingleChannel(byte[] pixels, bool fromAlpha)

docs.summary: Moves one channel into red, alpha when `fromAlpha`, leaving the rest black and opaque.
The red channel of every pixel.

members.name: DilateTransparent
members.signature: public static void DilateTransparent(byte[] pixels, int width, int height)

docs.summary: Fills the colour of fully transparent pixels from their visible neighbours, so filtering and compression across an edge do not pull in whatever colour the invisible pixels held. Alpha is untouched.
